reason: Schedule is fine. The probe fails the value lens because the information it buys is mostly available at no slot cost, and it would not change the action taken. (1) Zero-slot bounds already exist. exp49/exp51 have no REPAIR_DEADLINE guard (grep of experiments/exp49_edgefilter, exp51_coordhead) and share x138's detector/TTA GPU phase. They scored, so runtime <= latency (7.0-7.2 h for #29/#30; v_ensembles-and-private_x138-budget-aware-deadline_schedule.notes.md l.6). With dummy costs from browser_intel s.6.0B (GPU+ILP 256-281 s per clip over 2 shards, startup ~440 s), that gives N <= ~135-160 depending on the exp48/49 per-clip repair time (N1 step 0 fixes it from logs). x138's own 0.953 gives N <~ 190, since all repairs start after the GPU phase. So the F>19k bucket is essentially empty and the 16-19k bucket is mostly excluded before the probe runs. (2) The idea misses a zero-slot measurement arriving the same evening. #34 and #35 were submitted 24 min apart, share the GPU phase and differ only in repair cost (57 vs 123 s per clip on the dummies). With 10-minute polling, the latency difference estimates N to about +-20 if the guard did not fire. #35 scored vs timed out also answers the insertion-timeout question directly. (3) The actions the buckets gate are weakly dominant in every N world: N1 parallel repair (byte-identical CSV), the divinsert deadline guard, fail-soft wrappers. Guard-free finals (exp51/exp52) are already proven complete on the hidden set. P(the probe flips a decision) is ~0.05-0.1, not 0.25-0.35, so decision value ~0 for a non-zero policy cost (LB metadata probing needs the user's decision). (4) The mechanics are unverified. The Kaggle scorer wrapper is not in the repo (tools/official has only the metric). A 'valid' CSV with one node and no edges per dataset may itself raise a scoring error (0/0 Jaccard), which would misread bucket 1 as bucket 3. The distinct error texts are a guess (FAQ not read). The probe may queue behind the pending #34/#35, so the claimed speed advantage is unproven. (5) The bucket thresholds assume dummy per-clip speed and rho, the same assumptions under which the Data tab ('~199') conflicts with 0.953. A single N reading does not settle rho (private density), which drives the degraded share as much as N does (sim table).
fix_if_any: Demote to a conditional fallback; do not spend the 25 Sep slot by default. Do these first, all zero-slot. (a) N1 step 0: the local session pulls the exp48/49/51/56/57b logs; the agent turns per-clip repair seconds + the #28-#33 latencies into an N upper bound. (b) Tonight the local session polls `kaggle competitions submissions` every 10 min to time #34 and #35; N ~ (L35-L34)/66 s if neither guard fired, and #35 timeout vs scored is read directly. (c) Build N1 regardless of N; it is output-identical and dominant. Trigger the probe only if ALL of: N1 fails its dummy/sha test by 27 Sep, (a)+(b) still leave N in 130-170, and the user OKs LB metadata probing. Then use a 2-state design at ONE threshold chosen for the finals decision (e.g. F = 15,000): below it, write a CSV with 2 nodes + 1 edge per dataset (avoids a degenerate 0/0 in the scorer); above it, raise. Wrap the shape reader so that any internal error writes NO CSV ('CSV not found'), reserved as 'probe bug', never read as a bucket. Read shapes from each array's zarr.json (JSON only) and fall back to T=100 x clip count. Pre-register the table in CONTEXT.md. Before trusting the error texts, read the Code Competition FAQ in the browser.
realistic_public_gain: 0 (by design the probe scores ~0 or errors).
realistic_private_gain: ~0 (<= +0.0005 expected). N1 captures the runtime-safety gain whatever the probe says, and #34/#35 latencies plus step 0 supply most of the N information for free. The probe only matters in the narrow world where N1 cannot be built AND the latencies are inconclusive (P ~0.05-0.1).
critical_path: If triggered on 25 Sep. 12:30-14:00 UTC, agent container: ~30-line probe script + fake-zarr tests per bucket + table in a task card, pushed to git (0.5 h). 15:40 UTC, local session: check #34 in `kaggle competitions submissions`; if still pending and step 0 inconclusive, ask the user for an explicit OK. ~15:50, local session: `kaggle kernels push` of a CPU kernel attached only to the competition data; commit run on the 4 dummies ~2-5 min, must print F=400/N=4 and write the valid CSV. ~16:00: submit on the spare 25 Sep slot (it has no other use: vitaliineibauer has ~0 GPU-h until 00:00 UTC). Hidden rerun takes minutes, plus unknown queueing behind the pending #34/#35 (possibly until one finishes, ~16-20 UTC). Read the status text on the Submissions page in Chrome (the CLI may show only 'error'); apply the pre-registered table. Earliest outcome ~16:30 UTC, likely 17-20 UTC, the same window as #34/#35 themselves. In the recommended conditional form: any 26-28 Sep slot, same ~1 h of work, outcome within ~1-3 h, far ahead of 29 Sep 10:00 UTC.
